Key to the Broadleaf Trees of the Cottonwood Bottoms

1a. Leaves opposite on the twig ........................................ 2
1b. Leaves alternate on the twig ....................................... 4
2a. Leaves simple, palmately lobed, the lobes sharply
    toothed ................... Acer glabrum Torr. (Rocky Mountain maple)
2b. Leaves pinnately compound .......................................... 3
3a. Leaflets 3 to 5, coarsely toothed or shallowly lobed; fruit a
    paired samara ........................... Acer negundo L. (boxelder)
3b. Leaflets 5 to 9, finely toothed; fruit a single pad-
    dle-shaped samara ........... Fraxinus pennsylvanica Marshall, p. 118
4a. Buds covered by a single cap-like scale; fruit a capsule
    releasing cottony seeds ................................ Salix, p. 131
4b. Buds with several overlapping scales ............................... 5
5a. Bark peeling in papery sheets; fruit a small cone-like catkin ...... 6
5b. Bark smooth or furrowed, not peeling; fruit a capsule releasing
    cottony seeds ...................................................... 7
6a. Bark white, peeling freely ..... Betula papyrifera Marshall (paper birch)
6b. Bark coppery brown and shiny, peeling
    little ......................... Betula occidentalis Hook. (water birch)
7a. Leaf stalk flattened from side to side, the leaves trembling
    in a light wind ....... Populus tremuloides Michx. (quaking aspen)
7b. Leaf stalk round in cross-section .................................. 8
8a. Leaves lance-shaped, less than 2.5 cm
    wide ...... Populus angustifolia E. James (narrowleaf cottonwood)
8b. Leaves egg-shaped to triangular, more than 4 cm wide ..... Populus
    balsamifera L. subsp. trichocarpa (Torr. & A. Gray) Brayshaw (black cottonwood)
